enso_odds.source: NOAA Climate Prediction Center, official ENSO probabilities
enso_odds.definition: El Nino: RONI at or above +0.5 C; La Nina: at or below -0.5 C. RONI is the 3-month mean sea surface temperature anomaly in the Nino-3.4 region (5N-5S, 170W-120W) minus the tropical-mean anomaly (20N-20S), rescaled; 1991-2020 base period.
enso_odds.note: CPC: a 0% chance is approximate - there is still a small, non-zero chance.

enso_strength.source: NOAA Climate Prediction Center, official ENSO strength probabilities
enso_strength.category_note: 'Index' is the Relative Oceanic Nino Index (RONI), a 3-month mean in degrees C. CPC names the bands weak, moderate, strong and very strong, in 0.5 C steps. CPC: strength does not necessarily match the strength of the impact.

mhw_forecast.source: NOAA Physical Sciences Laboratory, NMME marine heatwave forecast
mhw_forecast.subset_note: The newest forecast only (last start_time), fetched from PSL's DAP4 server one lead and band of latitudes at a time, because answers over 65,535 bytes came back corrupted; every piece's checksum is verified.
mhw_forecast.models: CanESM5, GEM5.2-NEMO, GFDL-SPEAR-regridded, NASA-GEOSS2S, COLA-RSMAS-CCSM4, COLA-RSMAS-CESM1, NCEP-CFSv2
mhw_forecast.note: Chance that the month's average sea surface temperature is in a marine heatwave: above the 90th percentile of 1991-2020 anomalies for that time of year (3-month window), computed from the North American Multi-Model Ensemble, with each model judged against its own forecast climate. Kept with the long-term warming trend (not detrended), so it asks the same question as the atlas's current heatwave layer (NOAA Coral Reef Watch, fixed climatology); the detrended version asks 'hot even for today's warmer ocean' and mostly gives lower odds. Per zone: the area-weighted (cos latitude) mean, and the maximum, over the 1-degree cells whose centres fall inside the zone or on its edge; land, sea-ice and blank cells excluded. 'approx' zones have no ocean cell centre inside them and use the ocean cells their outline passes through (approx_basis 'overlap') or the nearest ocean cell within 1.5 degrees ('nearest'). The first month is the month the forecast started in. Models run 9-11 months ahead, so the last months rest on fewer models. PSL calls these forecasts experimental.
